evidence.reason: The finding asks to fsync the record-directory (parent) after creating the run directory, claiming admission is claimed before the new directory entry is durable. The cited region is `claim_run_dir`, whose only durability-relevant action is `self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)` at line 612; the code syncs receipts via `durable_write` later (line 598) but nowhere in the shown flow does it sync `base` after the mkdir. That is an accurate description of the code, but the asserted failure mode is not an implementation error against the current contract. The contract's CRQ section and the linked runtime-ownership/deployment sections govern slot scheduling, admission, and ownership hints; durable_write semantics and parent-directory fsync are not specified there, and the pinned contract's item 14 explicitly frames such residual trust/durability properties as recorded limits rather than defects unless they implicate the item 17 blocking checks or item 18 merge bar. No supplied source shows that `base` can be on a separate filesystem from the run dir (it is a subdirectory of `base`, so same filesystem by construction; the claim of cross-filesystem loss is unsupported), and the record base existing/being created is not shown to require its own parent-entry persistence under any current requirement. The behavior described (mkdir + later receipt write) is ordinary crash-window exposure, not a contract violation, and adding mandatory fsync/failure-refusal for the parent directory would enlarge the durability/approval scope beyond the pinned contract rather than repair existing intended behavior. Consequently the finding is not a valid defect on this tip; an opportunity to harden crash durability is advisory.
